bundleBaseline.measuredAt: 2026-08-10, after deferring the seed structure catalogue out of the entry chunk
bundleBaseline.entryBudgetRationale: Budget stays 1024 KiB; the entry now measures 841.88 kB raw / 280.08 kB gzip, 182.7 kB below the wave-3 baseline it replaces. The 1024 KiB was set when wave 3 doubled the curated atlas (176 → 371 islands), because the growth is L0 atlas DATA rather than a new runtime: atlas.ts loads eagerly on purpose so the first frame is a real map with no round trip, and every island's question (`qfocus`) must be present offline since the chart's hover card and the connection-field search both read it from the L0 projection via api/fallback.ts. Deferring qfocus to atlas-detail was measured (36% of the L0 payload; it lands the entry at 914KiB) and rejected — it leaves the no-server readable twin with a questionless island card, which the resilience invariant forbids. What DID move is the seed structure catalogue: structures.ts plus its two wave expansion modules, ~261KiB, reached the entry through static imports of api/structureFallback from two eager screens and through a two-line `slugOfOp` helper that used to live in the same module. That data is needed only once a reader opens the structure lens, so it now loads through import() as its own 294.18 kB chunk. Note the failure that preceded this: the wave-3 structure mappings (commit c97e625) pushed the entry to 1108.9 KiB — 85 KiB over — and it went unnoticed because `pnpm build` is in neither `pnpm -r test` nor `pnpm typecheck`, so every gate stayed green while the release build was broken. Naming the modules in guardEntryChunk's ENTRY_FORBIDDEN list is what makes the next occurrence say what leaked instead of only that the total grew.
